# 1\. Introduction

## 1.1 Purpose

This Software Requirements Specification establishes the requirements and quality expectations for an AI Research Paper Recommendation System. It provides a clear baseline for design, implementation, testing, and evaluation.

## 1.2 Problem Statement

Students and researchers often spend substantial time searching large academic collections. Keyword-only search can produce irrelevant results or miss papers using different terminology. The proposed system combines search with AI-assisted personalization and paper similarity to improve literature discovery.

## 1.3 Scope

The system provides authentication, profile and research-interest management, academic-paper search, personalized recommendations, paper details, bookmarking, feedback, history, and administration. The recommendation engine may use content-based similarity, NLP features, metadata, and user interactions.

## 1.4 Intended Audience

Developers, testers, faculty/project guides, administrators, students, researchers, and other project stakeholders.

# 2\. Overall Description

## 2.1 Product Perspective

The solution is a web-based recommendation platform comprising a presentation layer, backend/API layer, recommendation engine, database, and optional external academic-data integrations.

## 2.2 Major Functions

- User registration and authentication.
- Profile and research-interest management.
- Paper search, filtering, and detailed viewing.
- Personalized recommendation generation and ranking.
- Bookmarking and recommendation feedback.
- Search/recommendation history.
- Administrative management of users and paper records.

## 2.3 User Classes

Student/Researcher: discovers literature, receives recommendations, saves papers, and provides feedback. Administrator: manages users, paper records, and system data.

## 2.4 Assumptions

- Users have a modern web browser and network access.
- Paper metadata is available from a maintained database, dataset, or approved API.
- Recommendation quality depends on the quality of paper metadata and interaction data.

# 3\. Functional Requirements

| ID    | Requirement        | Specification                                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-01 | Registration       | Allow new users to create an account.                                               |
| FR-02 | Authentication     | Authenticate registered users and support secure logout.                            |
| FR-03 | Profile Management | Allow users to maintain profile and research interests.                             |
| FR-04 | Paper Search       | Support keyword search and filters such as author, topic, year, and category.       |
| FR-05 | Paper Details      | Display available title, authors, abstract, keywords, year, venue, and source link. |
| FR-06 | Recommendations    | Generate a ranked list of relevant papers using available user/paper information.   |
| FR-07 | Explanation        | Show a concise matching topic, keyword, or similarity reason where feasible.        |
| FR-08 | Bookmarking        | Allow authenticated users to save and remove papers.                                |
| FR-09 | Feedback           | Allow users to rate or provide feedback.                                            |
| FR-10 | History            | Maintain relevant search and recommendation history.                                |
| FR-11 | Administration     | Allow authorized administrators to manage users and paper records.                  |
| FR-12 | Error Handling     | Validate inputs and return meaningful errors for failed operations.                 |

# 4\. Non-Functional Requirements

| ID     | Attribute       | Specification                                                                      |
| ------ | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NFR-01 | Performance     | Provide responsive search and recommendation behavior under expected project load. |
| NFR-02 | Security        | Use secure password hashing and authentication/role-based authorization.           |
| NFR-03 | Usability       | Provide a responsive, consistent, and easy-to-navigate interface.                  |
| NFR-04 | Reliability     | Handle invalid input and common service failures gracefully.                       |
| NFR-05 | Scalability     | Support growth in users, papers, and recommendation algorithms.                    |
| NFR-06 | Maintainability | Keep frontend, backend, recommendation logic, and data access modular.             |
| NFR-07 | Privacy         | Restrict user profile and activity data to authorized access.                      |

# 5\. External Interface Requirements

## 5.1 User Interface

The interface should include authentication, dashboard, paper search, recommendation feed, paper details, bookmarks/history, profile settings, and an administrator dashboard.

## 5.2 Software Interfaces

- Frontend: React or equivalent modern web framework.
- Backend: Node.js/Express, Flask, or equivalent REST API framework.
- Database: MongoDB, PostgreSQL, or equivalent.
- Recommendation Engine: Python/ML service or modular backend component.
- Optional academic-paper APIs or curated datasets.

## 5.3 Hardware Interfaces

No specialized hardware is required.

# 6\. Data Requirements

| Entity         | Representative Attributes                                             |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| User           | user_id, name, email, password_hash, interests, role, created_at      |
| Research Paper | paper_id, title, authors, abstract, keywords, year, venue, source_url |
| Bookmark       | bookmark_id, user_id, paper_id, created_at                            |
| Feedback       | feedback_id, user_id, paper_id, rating, comment, created_at           |
| History        | history_id, user_id, query/recommendation data, timestamp             |

# 7\. System Architecture

- Presentation Layer — responsive web interface.
- Application/API Layer — authentication, search, bookmarks, feedback, history, and administration.
- Recommendation Layer — similarity calculation, personalization, ranking, and optional NLP/ML processing.
- Data Layer — users, papers, interactions, and system records.
- External Integration Layer — optional academic-paper metadata providers.

| UC-07 | Rate / Feedback       | Student/Researcher | Submit feedback.                      | Feedback stored.             |
| UC-08 | View History          | Student/Researcher | Open history.                         | Relevant history displayed.  |
| UC-09 | Manage Users & Papers | Administrator      | Maintain authorized records.          | Changes applied.             |

# 10\. Security Requirements

- Passwords shall never be stored in plaintext.
- Protected operations shall require authentication.
- Administrator functions shall use role-based authorization.
- Validate and sanitize user input at API boundaries.
- Use HTTPS in production.
- Restrict personal activity and profile information to authorized access.

# 11\. Future Enhancements

- Transformer-based semantic embeddings.
- Explainable recommendation scores.
- Privacy-conscious collaborative filtering.
- Research trend detection.
- Additional academic indexes and metadata services.
- Personalized alerts for newly available papers.

# 12\. Acceptance Criteria

- Users can register, authenticate, and manage interests.
- Users can search, filter, and view papers.
- The system returns ranked recommendations.
- Users can bookmark papers and provide feedback.
- Authenticated users can access appropriate history.
- Administrators can manage users and paper records.
- Invalid input and common failures are handled gracefully.

# 13\. Conclusion

The AI Research Paper Recommendation System provides a structured and extensible platform for academic literature discovery. This SRS establishes a professional baseline for implementation, testing, evaluation, and future enhancement.
